title: probing-provision-controller-and-burst-inspector
author: Maya Alvarez
description:
Motivation: In highly elastic dedicated fleets we occasionally observe optimistic reservations that look good from passive metrics but collapse under microbursts. This PR introduces a light-weight active probing layer (ProbeProvisionController) that issues short-lived capacity probes and blends their results into a sliding reservation window. The probe stream provides higher-fidelity headroom estimates and allows graceful throttling when observed usable capacity diverges from statistical reservations.

What this changes (high level): Adds a ProbeProvisionController in the dedicated control plane that runs tenant-scoped micro-probes, a BurstInspector telemetry component that reports probe-derived signals, and a small simulation harness used to validate fairness across tenants and burst patterns. The blended reservation is a time-decayed average that mixes soft reservations, recent probe headroom samples, and a safety floor based on node-level allocatable.

Key features: 1) Probe-based headroom metric (probe_success_rate, probe_headroom_ms, probe_tail_latency_p90) emitted per-tenant and per-fleet. 2) Sliding reservation blender with configurable decay window and probe weight (config: reservation.decay_window_seconds, reservation.probe_weight). 3) BurstInspector endpoint for metrics ingestion and a Prometheus exporter that exposes blended_reservation_ratio and probe-derived stability score. 4) Simulator that runs multi-tenant scenarios to validate fairness and quantifies additional cost vs. SLA uplift. 5) Safe fallback: if probes fail or latency increases beyond threshold, controller falls back to conservative reservation and fast-fail throttling to prevent oversubscription.

Backward compatibility & rollout: ProbeProvisionController is feature gated (controller.features.probes = false by default). Helm chart value added under redwood-dedicated.values.yaml to opt-in. Migration path: opt-in in Canary fleet, monitor BurstInspector probe_success_rate and blended_reservation_ratio; default behavior unchanged for non-opted fleets.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for blender math and probe sampling; integration tests that run simulator scenarios (steady, spike, noisy node). Performance tests show median additional CPU < 3% on control plane and < 0.4% p99 scheduling latency change on serving path in our cluster-size 50 simulation. Added e2e smoke that verifies fallback when probes time out.

Risks and operational notes: Active probing increases control-plane traffic; probes are tiny (single RPCs with short TTL) and rate-limited per-tenant. We recommend progressive rollout by enabling probes for low-risk tenants first. Alerting: added alerts for probe_success_rate < 90% and blended_reservation_ratio drift > 15% for > 5m.

Related work: complements the existing headroom scheduler and reservation decayers (see ENG-15230). This PR also implements better observability hooks which are useful for upcoming proportional backfill work.

Documentation: Added design doc and operator runbook describing tuning knobs, required dashboards, and recommended rollout checklist.

Linked Linear: ENG-17482 (probe provisioning), ENG-17610 (burst telemetry). Jira ticket SUP-455 contains customer reproduction used to drive the probe approach.

review_comments: Daniel Park (2026-02-18): Nice approach. Two asks: 1) ensure probe rate limits are enforced per-tenant (not just global) and 2) please add a small benchmark showing controller CPU impact under 1000 tenants.
Maya Alvarez (2026-02-19): Added per-tenant token bucket & synthetic benchmark in simulator (see commit g7b9c1d). Updated runbook with suggested tenant rollout order.

Priya Singh (2026-02-22): Safety concern: the initial probe_weight default (0.5) looks optimistic. Recommend 0.2 until we get more field data. Also please expose a feature flag for fast-fail throttling threshold.
Maya Alvarez (2026-02-23): Lowered default probe_weight to 0.2 and added controller.features.probes.fast_fail_threshold (docs updated).
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-24): Tests look good. One nit: use context deadlines in simulator RPCs for deterministic failures.
Maya Alvarez (2026-02-25): Switched simulator RPCs to use deadlines; added an integration test that asserts fallback path when probes exceed deadline.
ci_checks: lint: initially failed (goimports), fixed in g7b9c1d and re-ran, passed
release_notes: Feature: Probe-based reservation blending (opt-in). Operators can enable controller.features.probes to smooth reservations using active probes. New telemetry: probe_success_rate, probe_headroom_ms, blended_reservation_ratio. Added operator runbook and Helm opt-in values. Safe fallback ensures no regression when probes are unreliable.
notes_for_sre: Enable probes only in canary clusters. Watch Alert: probe_success_rate < 90% and blended_reservation_ratio drift > 15%. Default probe_weight=0.2; increase only after 48h of stable telemetry. Control-plane CPU impact observed ~3% in tests; ensure control-plane autoscaling buffer before enabling at fleet scale.
